title: Belgium's Budget Impasse Tests Coalition Cohesion and EU Fiscal Rules · 14 Oct
keywords: Belgium, federal budget, fiscal policy, budget deficit, austerity, Bart De Wever, European Commission, inflation, Eurostat, trade unions, public services, EU fiscal rules, Belgian politics, debt crisis, social protection
notes: Belgium's federal government has failed to agree on a package to close a projected budget gap of more than ten billion euros by 2029, forcing Prime Minister Bart De Wever to postpone his State of the Union address and raising questions about the coalition's durability. The deadlock arrives as Belgian inflation accelerates to 4.6 percent, intensifying a dispute over who should bear the costs of fiscal adjustment. National strikes and protests have disrupted public transport, schools, and broadcasters, signalling that the political and social stakes extend well beyond the negotiating table.
